schema.title: Agent
schema.description:
An agent running against Claude Code.

Far fewer knobs than OpenRouter's, and not because anything is
missing: Claude Code is an agent harness in its own right, so
the sampling decisions OpenRouter exposes are made inside it.
What it does expose is its tools: [`tools`](Self::tools) is the
exact set of built-ins the model is given, every switch stated,
passed to Claude Code as `--tools`;
[`dependencies`](Self::dependencies) is the other kind, the tool
containers the agent asks the caller to run for it.

tools.description:
The switchable built-in tools — each absent or `false` is
off, and the whole structure absent is every tool off. The
MCP tools and `Skill` are on regardless; see [`Tools`].

effort.description:
How much effort to spend thinking. Meaningful only with
[`thinking`](Self::thinking) on.

dependencies.description:
The tool containers this agent depends on, each a dependency
tool template the caller deploys and serves to it as an MCP
server, exactly as the SDK's [`Template`] states one: that
type's JSON Schema is what `GET /schema` states for this member,
and this list, unchanged, is what the registration answers —
one schema, from the one type, at both. Absent is none.

Tools.description:
The built-in tools Claude Code is given, every one stated.

Claude Code's `--tools` flag takes the exact set of built-ins the
model may call, and this is that set: a switch per tool, each an
`Option<bool>` where ABSENT IS OFF — the same as `false` — so
nothing is on by omission and a request names only what it
turns on. The harness renders the `true` switches as the flag's
list, in this order, after the always-on names.

Always on, no switch: the `mcp__*` tools — the caller's own
tools, served through the proxy — are not built-ins and are
present whatever `--tools` says: the tool channel is what the
protocol is built around. Beside them the harness always lists
the four MCP resource built-ins (`ListMcpResources`,
`ReadMcpResource`, `ReadMcpResourceDir`, `RefreshMcpTools` — the
caller's resources, through the same proxy), `Skill` (skills are
the directories mounted under `~/.claude/skills`; the tool is
offered whether or not any are, and a call names a skill that is
not there fails as "unknown skill"), and `ToolSearch`, by which
the model loads deferred tools' schemas.

Always off, no switch: `LSP` (nothing in the image installs a
language server). Nor does a switch exist for what cannot work
in the container, which the harness never lists:
`AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode`,
`ExitPlanMode`, `ProposeGoal` and `ProposeSkills` (a call waits
on a user who is not there); `CronCreate`, `CronDelete`,
`CronList` and `ScheduleWakeup` (the container does not outlive
the run); `Artifact`, `Projects`, `ClaudeDesign`, `RemoteTrigger`,
`PushNotification`, `SendFeedback`, `ReadNotifications`,
`ShowOnboardingRolePicker` and `EndConversation` (claude.ai
account and host features). Nor for the legacy names the binary
still answers to (`MultiEdit`, `BashOutput`, `KillShell`): they
are the old spellings of switches here.

Whether the pinned build honors every name here under `-p` with
stream-json input is a live-run check, not a promise of this
type; the names are as the runtime spells them.

bash.description:
`Bash`: runs a command, with an optional timeout and
optionally in the background.

read.description:
`Read`: reads a file by absolute path, with `offset` and `limit`
for large files and `pages` for PDFs.

notebook_edit.description: `NotebookEdit`: replaces, inserts or deletes one Jupyter cell.

grep.description:
`Grep`: ripgrep over the workspace (ripgrep ships with the
binary).

task.description:
`Task` (also spelled `Agent`): launches a sub-agent. Its chunks
reach the run's stream attributed by `parent_tool_call_id`.
Local sub-agents only: `isolation: remote` needs a cloud
environment the container has no account for.

task_output.description:
`TaskOutput`: reads the output of a background task, blocking
or not.

task_stop.description: `TaskStop`: stops a background task by id.

monitor.description:
`Monitor`: watches a command's stdout lines or a WebSocket's
frames as events.

workflow.description:
`Workflow`: runs a deterministic multi-agent orchestration
script.

task_create.description: `TaskCreate`: creates an entry on the session's task board.

report_findings.description: `ReportFindings`: reports code-review findings as a typed list.

repl.description:
`REPL`: runs JavaScript with persistent state and top-level
await.

web_fetch.description:
`WebFetch`: fetches a URL and runs a prompt over the content.
Needs outbound network from the container.

web_search.description:
`WebSearch`: searches the web, with domain allow and block
lists. Needs outbound network from the container.

enter_worktree.description:
`EnterWorktree`: creates or switches into a git worktree. Needs
the workspace to be a git repository.

exit_worktree.description: `ExitWorktree`: leaves the worktree, keeping or removing it.

Effort.description: How much effort the model should spend before answering.

oneOf.description: As much as the model will spend.

Template.description:
One tool container an agent's program depends on: everything the
caller needs to deploy it, as fields and not as words. A tool
container depends on nothing.

A [`Container`](crate::shared::containers::request::Container) is
an image, two limits, mounts and arguments. The image, the limits
and the arguments are here, member for member. The mounts are not
the caller's volumes — a volume is named in the caller's own
listing, and a tool that named one would be dictating the caller's
storage — but, for a transient tool alone, the AGENT's own files
and directories, each a path in the agent container served live at
a path in the tool container: the caller serves the agent
container, a `containers::fuse_serve` of the path, and mounts the tool,
a `fuse::mount` answered from it. [`mode`](Self::mode) says which
of the two modes the dependency is — a transient tool of the
agent's run, with those mounts, or a service the caller keeps,
with a scope — see [`Mode`]; and [`permissions`](Self::permissions)
what its account may do — grants that name nothing, so the
template is the same on every daemon it reaches, and among them
the word `self`, which reaches the agent a transient tool is the
dependency of and every agent attached to a service.

There are no instructions. What a template cannot say — the
provider the tool runs on, the volumes it is given, the account's
name — is the caller's, and the caller needs no prose to choose it.
The daemon's own tool templates are another thing: a record the
daemon keeps, named by a hash, made by a request; this is what an
image declares and a caller deploys.

There is no name. A dependency is named by its ID: the lowercase
hexadecimal SHA-256 of its [`canonical`](crate::shared::canonical)
bytes — this template as compact JSON, absent members omitted,
the image's `references` absent too, every object key sorted at
every depth, the `arguments` included, the `mode` and its
members among the keys — sixty-four characters, which the caller
computes over [`hashed`](Self::hashed). Two declarations with one
id are one dependency, and a list that declares one twice is
refused; the same template deployed for the same agent, on
whatever provider, is the same dependency, and the same service
template declared under the same scope key, by whatever agent, is
the same service. The caller labels the tool's MCP tools by the id
when it merges lists, and the program knows which tool serves each
by the keys under `_meta`, see [`shared::mcp`](crate::shared::mcp).

image.description:
The image: a digest and its references, as a
`containers::tools::run` request names one.

memory.description: The memory the tool container needs, in bytes.

disk.description: The bytes the tool container may write, in bytes.

arguments.description:
The arguments the tool container is registered with — the
`arguments` of the run request that makes it, verbatim.

permissions.description:
What the tool's account may do, as grants that name nothing:
see [`Grant`]. The caller gives the tool an account holding
exactly these. Absent when empty, and then the tool may do
nothing through the daemon.

oneOf.description: A tool for the agent's run: `"mode":"transient"`.

fuse_file_mounts.description:
Files of the agent container served live into the tool
container, one each over FUSE: see [`Mount`]. The agent's
path names a file; the tool's path is where it appears.
Absent when empty.

fuse_directory_mounts.description:
Directories of the agent container served live into the
tool container, one each over FUSE: see [`Mount`]. The
agent's path names a directory, whose whole tree the tool
sees; the tool's path is where it appears. Absent when
empty.

scope.description:
How far the service is shared, and its database with it:
see [`Scope`].

Image.description:
The image, by its manifest digest and the references under which
its bytes may be fetched — what
[`images::check`](crate::provider::endpoints::images::check::client::request::Frame)
asks about, so a check that came back available names an image a
run can ask for, with nothing to translate between them.

# The digest is the image

A digest cannot be repointed at different content, so an image
means the same bytes every time, wherever they come from. That is
the whole of what the wire asserts: the provider runs the image
the digest names and no other. The references are not the image:
the same bytes sit under different names on different registries,
and an id that hashes an image hashes it with none — see
[`hashed`](Self::hashed).

# Who supplies the bytes is the provider's

A provider looks in what it holds first, by digest alone — among
which are the images the caller
[built](crate::provider::endpoints::images::build) on it, and no
other caller's. Failing that it may ask any referenced registry its own policy lists, with
the credential it holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one
it does not; and it may take the image from the caller — asking on
the run scope whether the caller holds it and, when it does, for
its manifest and blobs, see [`oci`](crate::shared::containers::oci).
Which of those, in what order, is the provider's policy, and a
caller learns only whether the run happened. A caller need not
hold what it names; one that does answers so when asked.

digest.description:
The manifest digest, `<algorithm>:<hex>`.

What identifies the image: a runtime hashes what it pulls, so
a source serving other bytes under it fails before anything
runs.

references.description:
Where the bytes may be fetched, each a registry and a path
there: see [`Reference`]. Absent when there are none, and then
the provider has only what it holds and what the caller holds.

Reference.description:
One place the bytes an image's digest names may be fetched from: a
registry, and the repository path there. A reference locates and
does not identify — the digest does — so an image may carry none,
one or several, and two images with one digest are one image
whatever each lists. A provider asks a referenced registry only
where its own policy lists that registry, with the credential it
holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one it does not.

registry.description:
The registry's host, as a reference names it before its first
`/`: `docker.io`, `ghcr.io`, `registry.example.com:5000`. No
scheme and no path.

name.description:
The repository path at that registry — `library/nginx`,
`myorg/myimage`. No host and no tag: the image is
`<registry>/<name>@<digest>` there.

It lands in a reference by concatenation wherever a provider
pulls from, so a provider refuses one that is not a repository
path and normalizes nothing.

Mount.description:
A path of the agent container, mounted at a path of the tool
container over FUSE: source before destination, the order a mount
reads in everywhere else. Which of the two it is — a file or a
directory — is which list of the [`Template`](super::Template) it
is on.

The caller serves the agent container's path live — a
`containers::fuse_serve` of it, or of the directory holding a file —
and makes the mount in the tool container as a FUSE mount answered
from that FUSE serve, so every read, write, listing, removal, rename and
new directory the tool makes is one ask answered from the agent's
own filesystem, where the agent sees it at once. Nothing is copied:
the two containers share the path for as long as both run.

agent_path.description:
Where it is in the agent container, as path components from the
agent container's root — the shape every path in this crate
takes. No component is empty, `.` or `..`, and the path is not
the root: a file on the file list, a directory on the directory
list.

tool_path.description:
Where it appears in the tool container, as path components from
the tool container's root, under the rules a
[`Container`](crate::shared::containers::request::Container)
states for its mounts: not the root, no other mount's, inside
no other mount's, and no other mount's inside it.

Scope.description:
What a service tool is one of: one per parent agent, one per
parent agent template, or one for every agent that declares it,
whatever template they are made from. The scope names the service
— the same template declared under the same scope key is the same
service, joined and not made again — and names its database scope
with it, so what a service holds is shared exactly as far as the
service is. Snake case on the wire: `"instance"`,
`"template"`, `"global"`.

oneOf.description:
One service per parent agent: the service deployed for one
agent is its own, with a database of its own, and two agents'
services of this template never see each other's. The scope a
transient tool has without saying so.

One service per parent agent template: every agent made from
the same agent template that declares this template is
attached to one service, which holds one database, so what one
writes the others read.

One service for the template, full stop: every agent that
declares it, from whatever agent template, is attached to the
one service, and its database is one for all of them.

Grant.description:
One grant that names nothing: a permission over one kind of thing
the daemon holds, reaching by tags alone. Externally tagged by the
kind's name — one object with one member, `{"agents":…}`,
`{"volumes":…}` — whose value is that kind's
[`Permission`](agents::Permission), in one of the shapes
[`permission`](crate::shared::permission) states. Snake case on the
wire: `"agents"`, `"agents_templates"`, `"standalone_tools"`,
`"standalone_tools_templates"`, `"dependency_tools"`,
`"providers_outgoing"`,
`"providers_incoming"`, `"providers_daemons"`, `"accounts"`,
`"roles"`, `"volumes"`, `"postgres"` — the kinds of
the daemon's [`Grant`](crate::daemon::grant::Grant), which is made
of these.

Permission.description:
What one grant over agents allows, in one of three shapes told
apart on the wire by their very form, as
[`permission`](crate::shared::permission) states them: a bare array
of [`Make`] actions; an object of [`Over`] actions and how far they
reach — every agent, the dependency's own, or by tags; or an object
of tagging actions, how far they reach, and which tags. An object
that is none of these — an action of one shape among another's, a
member missing, a `within` that is not `"any"`, `"self"` or a
[`Tags`] — does not decode.

anyOf.description:
To make: the [`Make`] actions held, as a bare array. Nothing is
judged but that the action is held.

Over agents that exist: the [`Over`] actions held, reaching
every one of them, the dependency's own agents, or only those
the [`Tags`] let through, read as a test.

within.description:
How far: `"any"`, `"self"`, or the tags as a test. See
[`Within`].

anyOf.description:
Tagging agents: putting tags on, taking them off, or both,
reaching every one or only those the [`Tags`] let through, and
touching any tag or only the ones listed.

within.description: How far: `"any"`, or the tags as a test.

Make.description:
The actions over agents that make one where there was none, which a
grant holds or does not and judges by nothing else. Snake case on
the wire: `"create"`.

Over.description:
The actions over agents that exist, which a grant reaches as far as
its `within` says. Snake case on the wire: `"get"`, `"delete"`,
`"edit"`, `"message"`, `"logs"`, `"list"`, `"download"`, `"upload"`,
`"transfer"`, `"filetree"`.

oneOf.description:
Send one a message, as
[`agents::message`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::message)
does.

Send the client files out of one, as
[`agents::download`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::download)
does.

Put files into one, as
[`agents::upload`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::upload)
does, and as a transfer landing in one does.

Copy files out of one, as
[`agents::transfer`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::transfer)
does; where they land is judged by its own grant.

Watch one's container whole, as
[`agents::filetree`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::filetree)
does.

Tags.description:
Which of a kind a grant reaches, by their tags: those carrying
every one of `all_tags` and any one of `any_tags`. A member that
is empty is absent, and passes everything; both empty is every one
of the kind, which `"any"` says more plainly. Read as a TEST, as
the daemon reads a `within`: a thing passes when it passes every
member given. The two words are the ones every list filter of the
daemon's already has, so a grant here and a grant of the daemon's
read tags the same way. No other member decodes: a `within` that
named something — `names`, `templates`, `creators` — would
otherwise read as no tags at all, which is everything, and a grant
must never widen by being misread.

all_tags.description:
Every one of these among the thing's tags. Absent when empty,
and then any tags.

any_tags.description:
Any one of these among the thing's tags; with `all_tags`, both
hold. Absent when empty, and then any tags.

Tagging.description:
Putting tags on, or taking them off: the actions of a tagging grant,
the same two for every kind that carries tags. Snake case on the
wire: `"tag"`, `"untag"`.

oneOf.description: Put tags on, as the kind's `tag` endpoint does.
Take tags off, as the kind's `untag` endpoint does.

Permission2.description:
What one grant over agent templates allows, in one of three shapes told
apart on the wire by their very form, as
[`permission`](crate::shared::permission) states them: a bare array
of [`Make`] actions; an object of [`Over`] actions and how far they
reach, by tags; or an object of tagging actions, how far they
reach, and which tags. An object that is none of these — an action
of one shape among another's, a member missing, a `within` that is
not `"any"` or a [`Tags`] — does not decode.

anyOf.description:
To make: the [`Make`] actions held, as a bare array. Nothing is
judged but that the action is held.

Over agent templates that exist: the [`Over`] actions held, reaching
every one of them, or only those the [`Tags`] let through,
read as a test.

within.description: How far: `"any"`, or the tags as a test.

anyOf.description:
Tagging agent templates: putting tags on, taking them off, or both,
reaching every one or only those the [`Tags`] let through, and
touching any tag or only the ones listed.

within.description: How far: `"any"`, or the tags as a test.

Make2.description:
The actions over agent templates that make one where there was none,
which a grant holds or does not and judges by nothing else. Snake
case on the wire: `"create"`.

Over2.description:
The actions over agent templates that exist, which a grant reaches
as far as its `within` says. Snake case on the wire: `"get"`,
`"attach"`, `"delete"`, `"list"`.

oneOf.description:
Attach a tool to every agent of one, or detach one, as
[`attach_agent_template`](crate::daemon::endpoints::standalone_tools::attach_agent_template)
and
[`detach_agent_template`](crate::daemon::endpoints::standalone_tools::detach_agent_template)
do; the tool is judged by an `attach` or a `detach` grant over
tools.

List them, as
[`agents::templates::list`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::templates::list)

schema.title: Agent
schema.description:
An agent running against Codex.

Few knobs, and not because anything is missing: Codex decides its
own sampling, its own tools and its own loop, and what it exposes
to a caller is the model, how hard it reasons and how it speaks,
whether it may search the web, and where it sends its requests.
How it logs in is not the agent's to say: the login is a mount or
the vault's (see [the module](super)). Each field is one config
key or flag, named in its
doc; every `Option` absent leaves that key unset, so Codex applies
its own default for the model — except [`web_search`](Self::web_search),
where absent is off, because nothing is on by omission.

model.description:
The model to run: `model` (`--model`), in the endpoint's own
naming.

effort.description:
How much effort the model spends reasoning:
`model_reasoning_effort`. See [`Effort`].

reasoning_summary.description:
How much of its reasoning the model says out loud:
`model_reasoning_summary`. What the stream's reasoning chunks
carry. See [`Summary`].

verbosity.description:
How long the model's answers run: `model_verbosity`. See
[`Verbosity`].

web_search.description:
Whether, and how, the model may search the web: `web_search`.
A capability of Codex itself rather than a tool of the
caller's — Codex performs the search and never calls out.
ABSENT IS `disabled`. See [`WebSearch`].

provider.description:
Where requests go instead of OpenAI: a `model_providers` entry
the harness writes and selects, its key the `OPENAI_API_KEY`
the run found. Absent is OpenAI's own endpoint. See
[`Provider`].

dependencies.description:
The tool containers this agent depends on, each a dependency
tool template the caller deploys and serves to it as an MCP
server, exactly as the SDK's [`Template`] states one: that
type's JSON Schema is what `GET /schema` states for this member,
and this list, unchanged, is what the registration answers —
one schema, from the one type, at both. Absent is none.

Effort.description:
How much effort the model spends before answering: Codex's
`model_reasoning_effort`, its five rungs as Codex spells them.
There is no `max`: `xhigh` is the top, and a model that has fewer
rungs takes the nearest it has.

oneOf.description: As much as the model will spend.

Summary.description:
How much of its reasoning the model says out loud: Codex's
`model_reasoning_summary`. What the run's reasoning chunks carry —
Codex streams the summary, never the raw reasoning, so this is
the whole of what a caller can see of the model thinking.

oneOf.description: No summary: the reasoning chunks stay empty.

Verbosity.description:
How long the model's answers run: Codex's `model_verbosity`,
honored by the models that take it (the reference names the GPT-5
family on the Responses API) and unset otherwise.

WebSearch.description:
Whether, and how, the model may search the web: Codex's
`web_search`, its four values as Codex spells them. Codex performs
the search itself — it is a capability of the upstream, not a tool
the caller serves — so a search never appears on the stream as
one of the caller's tool calls. The harness writes `disabled` when
the agent says nothing.

oneOf.description: Live fetches of the pages themselves.

Provider.description:
An endpoint other than OpenAI's: one `model_providers` entry the
harness writes as `model_providers.diverge` and selects with
`model_provider = "diverge"`. The entry's `env_key` is
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, the vault's, and its `wire_api` is `responses`,
the one value the configuration reference names — so the endpoint
must speak the Responses API, which the Diverge relay and every
upstream this protocol routes do.

Absent, Codex's own `openai` provider is used, with whatever
login the run found. Present, the entry is keyed by the
`OPENAI_API_KEY` the run found — a ChatGPT login speaks only to
OpenAI's own backend, and a provider beside one fails as itself,
in Codex's words.

Template.description:
One tool container an agent's program depends on: everything the
caller needs to deploy it, as fields and not as words. A tool
container depends on nothing.

A [`Container`](crate::shared::containers::request::Container) is
an image, two limits, mounts and arguments. The image, the limits
and the arguments are here, member for member. The mounts are not
the caller's volumes — a volume is named in the caller's own
listing, and a tool that named one would be dictating the caller's
storage — but, for a transient tool alone, the AGENT's own files
and directories, each a path in the agent container served live at
a path in the tool container: the caller serves the agent
container, a `containers::fuse_serve` of the path, and mounts the tool,
a `fuse::mount` answered from it. [`mode`](Self::mode) says which
of the two modes the dependency is — a transient tool of the
agent's run, with those mounts, or a service the caller keeps,
with a scope — see [`Mode`]; and [`permissions`](Self::permissions)
what its account may do — grants that name nothing, so the
template is the same on every daemon it reaches, and among them
the word `self`, which reaches the agent a transient tool is the
dependency of and every agent attached to a service.

There are no instructions. What a template cannot say — the
provider the tool runs on, the volumes it is given, the account's
name — is the caller's, and the caller needs no prose to choose it.
The daemon's own tool templates are another thing: a record the
daemon keeps, named by a hash, made by a request; this is what an
image declares and a caller deploys.

There is no name. A dependency is named by its ID: the lowercase
hexadecimal SHA-256 of its [`canonical`](crate::shared::canonical)
bytes — this template as compact JSON, absent members omitted,
the image's `references` absent too, every object key sorted at
every depth, the `arguments` included, the `mode` and its
members among the keys — sixty-four characters, which the caller
computes over [`hashed`](Self::hashed). Two declarations with one
id are one dependency, and a list that declares one twice is
refused; the same template deployed for the same agent, on
whatever provider, is the same dependency, and the same service
template declared under the same scope key, by whatever agent, is
the same service. The caller labels the tool's MCP tools by the id
when it merges lists, and the program knows which tool serves each
by the keys under `_meta`, see [`shared::mcp`](crate::shared::mcp).

image.description:
The image: a digest and its references, as a
`containers::tools::run` request names one.

memory.description: The memory the tool container needs, in bytes.

disk.description: The bytes the tool container may write, in bytes.

arguments.description:
The arguments the tool container is registered with — the
`arguments` of the run request that makes it, verbatim.

Image.description:
The image, by its manifest digest and the references under which
its bytes may be fetched — what
[`images::check`](crate::provider::endpoints::images::check::client::request::Frame)
asks about, so a check that came back available names an image a
run can ask for, with nothing to translate between them.

# The digest is the image

A digest cannot be repointed at different content, so an image
means the same bytes every time, wherever they come from. That is
the whole of what the wire asserts: the provider runs the image
the digest names and no other. The references are not the image:
the same bytes sit under different names on different registries,
and an id that hashes an image hashes it with none — see
[`hashed`](Self::hashed).

# Who supplies the bytes is the provider's

A provider looks in what it holds first, by digest alone — among
which are the images the caller
[built](crate::provider::endpoints::images::build) on it, and no
other caller's. Failing that it may ask any referenced registry its own policy lists, with
the credential it holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one
it does not; and it may take the image from the caller — asking on
the run scope whether the caller holds it and, when it does, for
its manifest and blobs, see [`oci`](crate::shared::containers::oci).
Which of those, in what order, is the provider's policy, and a
caller learns only whether the run happened. A caller need not
hold what it names; one that does answers so when asked.

digest.description:
The manifest digest, `<algorithm>:<hex>`.

What identifies the image: a runtime hashes what it pulls, so
a source serving other bytes under it fails before anything
runs.

references.description:
Where the bytes may be fetched, each a registry and a path
there: see [`Reference`]. Absent when there are none, and then
the provider has only what it holds and what the caller holds.

Reference.description:
One place the bytes an image's digest names may be fetched from: a
registry, and the repository path there. A reference locates and
does not identify — the digest does — so an image may carry none,
one or several, and two images with one digest are one image
whatever each lists. A provider asks a referenced registry only
where its own policy lists that registry, with the credential it
holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one it does not.

registry.description:

scheme and no path.

name.description:
The repository path at that registry — `library/nginx`,
`myorg/myimage`. No host and no tag: the image is
`<registry>/<name>@<digest>` there.

It lands in a reference by concatenation wherever a provider
pulls from, so a provider refuses one that is not a repository
path and normalizes nothing.

Mount.description:

container over FUSE: source before destination, the order a mount
reads in everywhere else. Which of the two it is — a file or a
directory — is which list of the [`Template`](super::Template) it
is on.

The caller serves the agent container's path live — a
`containers::fuse_serve` of it, or of the directory holding a file —
and makes the mount in the tool container as a FUSE mount answered
from that FUSE serve, so every read, write, listing, removal, rename and
new directory the tool makes is one ask answered from the agent's

the two containers share the path for as long as both run.

schema.title: Agent
schema.description:
An agent running against Hermes (Nous Research's agent harness).

Every field here is HONORABLE: it names a mechanism the container
actually has — a `config.yaml` key its harness writes before
Hermes starts, or a per-request field on the run it drives — and
nothing else made the cut. What Hermes cannot be told through its
wire is not here: no skill preloading (skills arrive as mounts
under `/root/.hermes/external-skills/`, one directory per skill
holding its `SKILL.md`, and Hermes indexes them itself — that
path, not its own `skills/`, which it writes into), no
temperature (Hermes has no
main-agent sampling key), no thinking-token budget (the
[`effort`](Self::effort) ladder is the whole reasoning
vocabulary).

provider.description:
The inference source, credentials and all — Hermes is
multi-provider by design, this picks which, and the pick
carries its own auth as arguments. See [`Provider`].

model.description: The model to run, in the provider's own naming.

system_prompt.description: The system prompt, applied per request.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort. Absent = the provider's own default;
[`none`](Effort::None) = explicitly disabled — Hermes's own
disable sentinel, which is why absence and `none` are
different facts. See [`Effort`].

toolsets.description:
Hermes's LOCAL capabilities, one switch each: an
`Option<bool>` where a tool takes nothing, that tool's own
argument structure where it does — absent is off either way,
and the whole structure absent is everything off. (The
caller's MCP tools ride beside these regardless, and the tool
containers the agent asks for are
[`dependencies`](Self::dependencies).) See [`Toolsets`].

dependencies.description:
The tool containers this agent depends on, each a dependency
tool template the caller deploys and serves to it as an MCP
server, exactly as the SDK's [`Template`] states one: that
type's JSON Schema is what `GET /schema` states for this member,
and this list, unchanged, is what the registration answers —
one schema, from the one type, at both. Absent is none.

Provider.description:
The inference source, credentials and all.

Untagged, discriminated by each variant's own `provider` constant
— the same discipline the [`Agent`](super::super::super::Agent)
union uses for `upstream`. One variant per provider because the
argument sets genuinely differ: most are a single key, but
bedrock is AWS credentials, vertex is a service-account document,
azure-foundry and custom carry their endpoints — and each key
applies through a different mechanism the variant's own docs
spell out.

CLOSED at the pin, deliberately: user plugins can extend Hermes's
registry, but the container runs stock Hermes, so the bundled set
is the whole vocabulary — minus `copilot-acp`, whose auth is not
Hermes's to hold (see [the module](super)). Rotating-OAuth
providers carry their state as RESOURCES rather than plain
values; the module doc says what that means.

Hermes's own `auto` — provider detection from whatever
credentials happen to be present — is deliberately NOT here, and
under auth-as-arguments it is not even coherent: the request
carries exactly one provider's credentials, so there is nothing
to detect.

Toolsets.description:
Per-toolset switches over Hermes's configurable checklist — the
list its own configuration wizard manages, closed at the pin,
and narrowed to what a REQUEST can actually make work.

Two field shapes, by whether the toolset takes arguments. A
toolset with nothing to configure is an `Option<bool>` where
ABSENT IS OFF — the same as `false` — so nothing is on by
omission and Hermes's own API-server defaults are never
consulted. A toolset with arguments is an `Option` of its own
structure — absent is off, present is the switch thrown on WITH
that tool's credentials and endpoint facts, each documented in
its own file with the mechanism the harness applies. Enabling a
tool without its prerequisites is not a protocol error — the
tools simply fail as themselves when used.

These are the agent's LOCAL capabilities: what Hermes itself can
do beside the conversation. The caller's MCP tools are not in
this vocabulary and never need to be — each configured MCP
server becomes its own toolset in Hermes automatically, and the
container always wires the caller's in. The SKILLS toolset is
not here either, on purpose: whether the agent can browse skills
follows from whether the request mounted any, not from a switch
that could contradict that fact.

What is deliberately ABSENT, and why, is [the module](super)'s
to say.

Template.description:
One tool container an agent's program depends on: everything the
caller needs to deploy it, as fields and not as words. A tool
container depends on nothing.

A [`Container`](crate::shared::containers::request::Container) is
an image, two limits, mounts and arguments. The image, the limits
and the arguments are here, member for member. The mounts are not
the caller's volumes — a volume is named in the caller's own
listing, and a tool that named one would be dictating the caller's
storage — but, for a transient tool alone, the AGENT's own files
and directories, each a path in the agent container served live at
a path in the tool container: the caller serves the agent
container, a `containers::fuse_serve` of the path, and mounts the tool,
a `fuse::mount` answered from it. [`mode`](Self::mode) says which
of the two modes the dependency is — a transient tool of the
agent's run, with those mounts, or a service the caller keeps,
with a scope — see [`Mode`]; and [`permissions`](Self::permissions)
what its account may do — grants that name nothing, so the
template is the same on every daemon it reaches, and among them
the word `self`, which reaches the agent a transient tool is the
dependency of and every agent attached to a service.

There are no instructions. What a template cannot say — the
provider the tool runs on, the volumes it is given, the account's
name — is the caller's, and the caller needs no prose to choose it.
The daemon's own tool templates are another thing: a record the
daemon keeps, named by a hash, made by a request; this is what an
image declares and a caller deploys.

There is no name. A dependency is named by its ID: the lowercase
hexadecimal SHA-256 of its [`canonical`](crate::shared::canonical)
bytes — this template as compact JSON, absent members omitted,
the image's `references` absent too, every object key sorted at
every depth, the `arguments` included, the `mode` and its
members among the keys — sixty-four characters, which the caller
computes over [`hashed`](Self::hashed). Two declarations with one
id are one dependency, and a list that declares one twice is
refused; the same template deployed for the same agent, on
whatever provider, is the same dependency, and the same service
template declared under the same scope key, by whatever agent, is
the same service. The caller labels the tool's MCP tools by the id
when it merges lists, and the program knows which tool serves each
by the keys under `_meta`, see [`shared::mcp`](crate::shared::mcp).

image.description:
The image: a digest and its references, as a
`containers::tools::run` request names one.

memory.description: The memory the tool container needs, in bytes.

disk.description: The bytes the tool container may write, in bytes.

arguments.description:
The arguments the tool container is registered with — the
`arguments` of the run request that makes it, verbatim.

permissions.description:
What the tool's account may do, as grants that name nothing:
see [`Grant`]. The caller gives the tool an account holding
exactly these. Absent when empty, and then the tool may do
nothing through the daemon.

oneOf.description: A tool for the agent's run: `"mode":"transient"`.

fuse_file_mounts.description:
Files of the agent container served live into the tool
container, one each over FUSE: see [`Mount`]. The agent's
path names a file; the tool's path is where it appears.
Absent when empty.

fuse_directory_mounts.description:
Directories of the agent container served live into the
tool container, one each over FUSE: see [`Mount`]. The
agent's path names a directory, whose whole tree the tool
sees; the tool's path is where it appears. Absent when
empty.

scope.description:
How far the service is shared, and its database with it:
see [`Scope`].

Image.description:
The image, by its manifest digest and the references under which
its bytes may be fetched — what
[`images::check`](crate::provider::endpoints::images::check::client::request::Frame)
asks about, so a check that came back available names an image a
run can ask for, with nothing to translate between them.

# The digest is the image

A digest cannot be repointed at different content, so an image
means the same bytes every time, wherever they come from. That is
the whole of what the wire asserts: the provider runs the image
the digest names and no other. The references are not the image:
the same bytes sit under different names on different registries,
and an id that hashes an image hashes it with none — see
[`hashed`](Self::hashed).

# Who supplies the bytes is the provider's

A provider looks in what it holds first, by digest alone — among
which are the images the caller
[built](crate::provider::endpoints::images::build) on it, and no
other caller's. Failing that it may ask any referenced registry its own policy lists, with
the credential it holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one
it does not; and it may take the image from the caller — asking on
the run scope whether the caller holds it and, when it does, for
its manifest and blobs, see [`oci`](crate::shared::containers::oci).
Which of those, in what order, is the provider's policy, and a
caller learns only whether the run happened. A caller need not
hold what it names; one that does answers so when asked.

digest.description:
The manifest digest, `<algorithm>:<hex>`.

What identifies the image: a runtime hashes what it pulls, so
a source serving other bytes under it fails before anything
runs.

references.description:
Where the bytes may be fetched, each a registry and a path
there: see [`Reference`]. Absent when there are none, and then
the provider has only what it holds and what the caller holds.

Reference.description:
One place the bytes an image's digest names may be fetched from: a
registry, and the repository path there. A reference locates and
does not identify — the digest does — so an image may carry none,
one or several, and two images with one digest are one image
whatever each lists. A provider asks a referenced registry only
where its own policy lists that registry, with the credential it
holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one it does not.

registry.description:
The registry's host, as a reference names it before its first
`/`: `docker.io`, `ghcr.io`, `registry.example.com:5000`. No
scheme and no path.

name.description:
The repository path at that registry — `library/nginx`,
`myorg/myimage`. No host and no tag: the image is
`<registry>/<name>@<digest>` there.

It lands in a reference by concatenation wherever a provider
pulls from, so a provider refuses one that is not a repository
path and normalizes nothing.

Mount.description:
A path of the agent container, mounted at a path of the tool
container over FUSE: source before destination, the order a mount
reads in everywhere else. Which of the two it is — a file or a
directory — is which list of the [`Template`](super::Template) it
is on.

The caller serves the agent container's path live — a
`containers::fuse_serve` of it, or of the directory holding a file —
and makes the mount in the tool container as a FUSE mount answered
from that FUSE serve, so every read, write, listing, removal, rename and
new directory the tool makes is one ask answered from the agent's
own filesystem, where the agent sees it at once. Nothing is copied:
the two containers share the path for as long as both run.

agent_path.description:
Where it is in the agent container, as path components from the
agent container's root — the shape every path in this crate
takes. No component is empty, `.` or `..`, and the path is not
the root: a file on the file list, a directory on the directory
list.

tool_path.description:
Where it appears in the tool container, as path components from
the tool container's root, under the rules a
[`Container`](crate::shared::containers::request::Container)
states for its mounts: not the root, no other mount's, inside
no other mount's, and no other mount's inside it.

Scope.description:
What a service tool is one of: one per parent agent, one per
parent agent template, or one for every agent that declares it,
whatever template they are made from. The scope names the service
— the same template declared under the same scope key is the same
service, joined and not made again — and names its database scope
with it, so what a service holds is shared exactly as far as the
service is. Snake case on the wire: `"instance"`,
`"template"`, `"global"`.

oneOf.description:
One service per parent agent: the service deployed for one
agent is its own, with a database of its own, and two agents'
services of this template never see each other's. The scope a
transient tool has without saying so.

One service per parent agent template: every agent made from
the same agent template that declares this template is
attached to one service, which holds one database, so what one
writes the others read.

One service for the template, full stop: every agent that
declares it, from whatever agent template, is attached to the
one service, and its database is one for all of them.

Grant.description:
One grant that names nothing: a permission over one kind of thing
the daemon holds, reaching by tags alone. Externally tagged by the
kind's name — one object with one member, `{"agents":…}`,
`{"volumes":…}` — whose value is that kind's
[`Permission`](agents::Permission), in one of the shapes
[`permission`](crate::shared::permission) states. Snake case on the
wire: `"agents"`, `"agents_templates"`, `"standalone_tools"`,
`"standalone_tools_templates"`, `"dependency_tools"`,
`"providers_outgoing"`,
`"providers_incoming"`, `"providers_daemons"`, `"accounts"`,
`"roles"`, `"volumes"`, `"postgres"` — the kinds of
the daemon's [`Grant`](crate::daemon::grant::Grant), which is made
of these.

Permission.description:
What one grant over agents allows, in one of three shapes told
apart on the wire by their very form, as
[`permission`](crate::shared::permission) states them: a bare array
of [`Make`] actions; an object of [`Over`] actions and how far they
reach — every agent, the dependency's own, or by tags; or an object
of tagging actions, how far they reach, and which tags. An object
that is none of these — an action of one shape among another's, a
member missing, a `within` that is not `"any"`, `"self"` or a
[`Tags`] — does not decode.

Tags.description:
Which of a kind a grant reaches, by their tags: those carrying
every one of `all_tags` and any one of `any_tags`. A member that
is empty is absent, and passes everything; both empty is every one
of the kind, which `"any"` says more plainly. Read as a TEST, as
the daemon reads a `within`: a thing passes when it passes every
member given. The two words are the ones every list filter of the
daemon's already has, so a grant here and a grant of the daemon's
read tags the same way. No other member decodes: a `within` that
named something — `names`, `templates`, `creators` — would
otherwise read as no tags at all, which is everything, and a grant
must never widen by being misread.

all_tags.description:
Every one of these among the thing's tags. Absent when empty,
and then any tags.

any_tags.description:
Any one of these among the thing's tags; with `all_tags`, both
hold. Absent when empty, and then any tags.

schema.title: Agent
schema.description:
An agent running against OpenRouter.

The widest parameter set of any upstream, because OpenRouter fronts
many providers and exposes what each of them accepts.

model.description: The model to route to, in OpenRouter's `vendor/name` form.

system_prompt.description:
The system prompt's text, sent as the conversation's leading
message.

top_logprobs.description:
How many alternatives to report per token. Absent means report
no log probabilities at all.

frequency_penalty.description: Penalise tokens by how often they have appeared.

logit_bias.description:
Per-token additive bias on the logits, keyed by token id.

An `IndexMap` rather than a `HashMap`: insertion order is
preserved, so the same bias set serializes identically every
time instead of shuffling between runs.

max_completion_tokens.description: Cap on generated tokens, counting reasoning tokens.

presence_penalty.description: Penalise tokens for having appeared at all, regardless of count.

max_tokens.description: Cap on generated tokens, excluding reasoning tokens.

min_p.description:
Minimum probability, relative to the most likely token, for a
token to be considered.

provider.description: Which backing providers to route to.

repetition_penalty.description: Multiplicative penalty on tokens already produced.

top_a.description:
Sample only from tokens above a threshold scaled by the most
likely token's probability.

top_k.description: Sample only from the k most likely tokens.

context_compression.description: What to do when the request exceeds the context window.

dependencies.description:
The tool containers this agent depends on, each a dependency
tool template the caller deploys and serves to it as an MCP
server, exactly as the SDK's [`Template`] states one: that
type's JSON Schema is what `GET /schema` states for this member,
and this list, unchanged, is what the registration answers —
one schema, from the one type, at both. Absent is none.

Stop.description:
Sequences that end generation when produced.

Untagged: one sequence goes on the wire as a bare string and
several as an array, matching what providers accept without a
caller having to wrap a single sequence in a list.

anyOf.description: One sequence.
Several. Providers typically cap this around four.

Provider.description:
Which backing providers OpenRouter may route to, and in what order.

OpenRouter fronts many providers for one model, and they differ in
price, throughput and quantization — so "which model" does not
fully determine what answers.

allow_fallbacks.description:
Whether to fall back to a provider outside the preferences when
none of them can serve the request.

require_parameters.description:
Only route to providers supporting every parameter sent.
Without this, unsupported parameters are silently dropped.

only.description: Route to these and no others.

quantizations.description:
Acceptable weight quantizations. A more aggressively quantized
model is cheaper and measurably different.

Reasoning.description:
How much the model should reason before answering, and how much of
that reasoning to report.

max_tokens.description:
A token budget for reasoning. Mutually exclusive with
[`effort`](Self::effort) on most models — a budget and a level
are two ways of saying the same thing.

effort.description: How hard to reason, as a level rather than a budget.

summary_verbosity.description: How much of the reasoning to summarise back.

ReasoningEffort.description: How hard the model should reason.

ReasoningSummaryVerbosity.description: How much of the reasoning to summarise in the response.

Verbosity.description:
How detailed the model's responses should be. A hint — not every
model honours it.

oneOf.description: As detailed as the model will go.

ContextCompression.description:
Which compression engine to enable when a request would otherwise
exceed the model's context window. Maps onto OpenRouter's
request-body `plugins` array.

oneOf.description:
Drops content from the middle of the conversation. The only
engine documented today.

Template.description:
One tool container an agent's program depends on: everything the
caller needs to deploy it, as fields and not as words. A tool
container depends on nothing.

A [`Container`](crate::shared::containers::request::Container) is
an image, two limits, mounts and arguments. The image, the limits
and the arguments are here, member for member. The mounts are not
the caller's volumes — a volume is named in the caller's own
listing, and a tool that named one would be dictating the caller's
storage — but, for a transient tool alone, the AGENT's own files
and directories, each a path in the agent container served live at
a path in the tool container: the caller serves the agent
container, a `containers::fuse_serve` of the path, and mounts the tool,
a `fuse::mount` answered from it. [`mode`](Self::mode) says which
of the two modes the dependency is — a transient tool of the
agent's run, with those mounts, or a service the caller keeps,
with a scope — see [`Mode`]; and [`permissions`](Self::permissions)
what its account may do — grants that name nothing, so the
template is the same on every daemon it reaches, and among them
the word `self`, which reaches the agent a transient tool is the
dependency of and every agent attached to a service.

There are no instructions. What a template cannot say — the
provider the tool runs on, the volumes it is given, the account's
name — is the caller's, and the caller needs no prose to choose it.
The daemon's own tool templates are another thing: a record the
daemon keeps, named by a hash, made by a request; this is what an
image declares and a caller deploys.

There is no name. A dependency is named by its ID: the lowercase
hexadecimal SHA-256 of its [`canonical`](crate::shared::canonical)
bytes — this template as compact JSON, absent members omitted,
the image's `references` absent too, every object key sorted at
every depth, the `arguments` included, the `mode` and its
members among the keys — sixty-four characters, which the caller
computes over [`hashed`](Self::hashed). Two declarations with one
id are one dependency, and a list that declares one twice is
refused; the same template deployed for the same agent, on
whatever provider, is the same dependency, and the same service
template declared under the same scope key, by whatever agent, is
the same service. The caller labels the tool's MCP tools by the id
when it merges lists, and the program knows which tool serves each
by the keys under `_meta`, see [`shared::mcp`](crate::shared::mcp).

image.description:
The image: a digest and its references, as a
`containers::tools::run` request names one.

memory.description: The memory the tool container needs, in bytes.

disk.description: The bytes the tool container may write, in bytes.

arguments.description:
The arguments the tool container is registered with — the
`arguments` of the run request that makes it, verbatim.

permissions.description:
What the tool's account may do, as grants that name nothing:
see [`Grant`]. The caller gives the tool an account holding
exactly these. Absent when empty, and then the tool may do
nothing through the daemon.

oneOf.description: A tool for the agent's run: `"mode":"transient"`.

fuse_file_mounts.description:
Files of the agent container served live into the tool
container, one each over FUSE: see [`Mount`]. The agent's
path names a file; the tool's path is where it appears.
Absent when empty.

fuse_directory_mounts.description:
Directories of the agent container served live into the
tool container, one each over FUSE: see [`Mount`]. The
agent's path names a directory, whose whole tree the tool
sees; the tool's path is where it appears. Absent when
empty.

scope.description:
How far the service is shared, and its database with it:
see [`Scope`].

Image.description:
The image, by its manifest digest and the references under which
its bytes may be fetched — what
[`images::check`](crate::provider::endpoints::images::check::client::request::Frame)
asks about, so a check that came back available names an image a
run can ask for, with nothing to translate between them.

# The digest is the image

A digest cannot be repointed at different content, so an image
means the same bytes every time, wherever they come from. That is
the whole of what the wire asserts: the provider runs the image
the digest names and no other. The references are not the image:
the same bytes sit under different names on different registries,
and an id that hashes an image hashes it with none — see
[`hashed`](Self::hashed).

# Who supplies the bytes is the provider's

A provider looks in what it holds first, by digest alone — among
which are the images the caller
[built](crate::provider::endpoints::images::build) on it, and no
other caller's. Failing that it may ask any referenced registry its own policy lists, with
the credential it holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one
it does not; and it may take the image from the caller — asking on
the run scope whether the caller holds it and, when it does, for
its manifest and blobs, see [`oci`](crate::shared::containers::oci).
Which of those, in what order, is the provider's policy, and a
caller learns only whether the run happened. A caller need not
hold what it names; one that does answers so when asked.

digest.description:
The manifest digest, `<algorithm>:<hex>`.

What identifies the image: a runtime hashes what it pulls, so
a source serving other bytes under it fails before anything
runs.

references.description:
Where the bytes may be fetched, each a registry and a path
there: see [`Reference`]. Absent when there are none, and then
the provider has only what it holds and what the caller holds.

Reference.description:
One place the bytes an image's digest names may be fetched from: a
registry, and the repository path there. A reference locates and
does not identify — the digest does — so an image may carry none,
one or several, and two images with one digest are one image
whatever each lists. A provider asks a referenced registry only
where its own policy lists that registry, with the credential it
holds for it, and ignores a reference naming one it does not.

registry.description:
The registry's host, as a reference names it before its first
`/`: `docker.io`, `ghcr.io`, `registry.example.com:5000`. No
scheme and no path.

name.description:
The repository path at that registry — `library/nginx`,
`myorg/myimage`. No host and no tag: the image is
`<registry>/<name>@<digest>` there.

It lands in a reference by concatenation wherever a provider
pulls from, so a provider refuses one that is not a repository
path and normalizes nothing.

Mount.description:
A path of the agent container, mounted at a path of the tool
container over FUSE: source before destination, the order a mount
reads in everywhere else. Which of the two it is — a file or a
directory — is which list of the [`Template`](super::Template) it
is on.

The caller serves the agent container's path live — a
`containers::fuse_serve` of it, or of the directory holding a file —
and makes the mount in the tool container as a FUSE mount answered
from that FUSE serve, so every read, write, listing, removal, rename and
new directory the tool makes is one ask answered from the agent's
own filesystem, where the agent sees it at once. Nothing is copied:
the two containers share the path for as long as both run.

agent_path.description:
Where it is in the agent container, as path components from the
agent container's root — the shape every path in this crate
takes. No component is empty, `.` or `..`, and the path is not
the root: a file on the file list, a directory on the directory
list.

tool_path.description:
Where it appears in the tool container, as path components from
the tool container's root, under the rules a
[`Container`](crate::shared::containers::request::Container)
states for its mounts: not the root, no other mount's, inside
no other mount's, and no other mount's inside it.

Scope.description:
What a service tool is one of: one per parent agent, one per
parent agent template, or one for every agent that declares it,
whatever template they are made from. The scope names the service
— the same template declared under the same scope key is the same
service, joined and not made again — and names its database scope
with it, so what a service holds is shared exactly as far as the
service is. Snake case on the wire: `"instance"`,
`"template"`, `"global"`.

oneOf.description:
One service per parent agent: the service deployed for one
agent is its own, with a database of its own, and two agents'
services of this template never see each other's. The scope a
transient tool has without saying so.

One service per parent agent template: every agent made from
the same agent template that declares this template is
attached to one service, which holds one database, so what one
writes the others read.

One service for the template, full stop: every agent that
declares it, from whatever agent template, is attached to the
one service, and its database is one for all of them.

Grant.description:
One grant that names nothing: a permission over one kind of thing
the daemon holds, reaching by tags alone. Externally tagged by the
kind's name — one object with one member, `{"agents":…}`,
`{"volumes":…}` — whose value is that kind's
[`Permission`](agents::Permission), in one of the shapes
[`permission`](crate::shared::permission) states. Snake case on the
wire: `"agents"`, `"agents_templates"`, `"standalone_tools"`,
`"standalone_tools_templates"`, `"dependency_tools"`,
`"providers_outgoing"`,
`"providers_incoming"`, `"providers_daemons"`, `"accounts"`,
`"roles"`, `"volumes"`, `"postgres"` — the kinds of
the daemon's [`Grant`](crate::daemon::grant::Grant), which is made
of these.

Permission.description:
What one grant over agents allows, in one of three shapes told
apart on the wire by their very form, as
[`permission`](crate::shared::permission) states them: a bare array
of [`Make`] actions; an object of [`Over`] actions and how far they
reach — every agent, the dependency's own, or by tags; or an object
of tagging actions, how far they reach, and which tags. An object
that is none of these — an action of one shape among another's, a
member missing, a `within` that is not `"any"`, `"self"` or a
[`Tags`] — does not decode.

anyOf.description:
To make: the [`Make`] actions held, as a bare array. Nothing is
judged but that the action is held.

Over agents that exist: the [`Over`] actions held, reaching
every one of them, the dependency's own agents, or only those
the [`Tags`] let through, read as a test.

within.description:
How far: `"any"`, `"self"`, or the tags as a test. See
[`Within`].

anyOf.description:
Tagging agents: putting tags on, taking them off, or both,
reaching every one or only those the [`Tags`] let through, and
touching any tag or only the ones listed.

within.description: How far: `"any"`, or the tags as a test.

Make.description:
The actions over agents that make one where there was none, which a
grant holds or does not and judges by nothing else. Snake case on
the wire: `"create"`.

Over.description:
The actions over agents that exist, which a grant reaches as far as
its `within` says. Snake case on the wire: `"get"`, `"delete"`,
`"edit"`, `"message"`, `"logs"`, `"list"`, `"download"`, `"upload"`,
`"transfer"`, `"filetree"`.

oneOf.description:

[`agents::message`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::message)
does.

Send the client files out of one, as
[`agents::download`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::download)
does.

Put files into one, as
[`agents::upload`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::upload)
does, and as a transfer landing in one does.

Copy files out of one, as
[`agents::transfer`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::transfer)
does; where they land is judged by its own grant.

Watch one's container whole, as
[`agents::filetree`](crate::daemon::endpoints::agents::filetree)
does.

Tags.description:
Which of a kind a grant reaches, by their tags: those carrying
every one of `all_tags` and any one of `any_tags`. A member that
is empty is absent, and passes everything; both empty is every one
of the kind, which `"any"` says more plainly. Read as a TEST, as
the daemon reads a `within`: a thing passes when it passes every
member given. The two words are the ones every list filter of the
daemon's already has, so a grant here and a grant of the daemon's
read tags the same way. No other member decodes: a `within` that
named something — `names`, `templates`, `creators` — would
otherwise read as no tags at all, which is everything, and a grant
must never widen by being misread.

all_tags.description:
Every one of these among the thing's tags. Absent when empty,
and then any tags.

any_tags.description:
Any one of these among the thing's tags; with `all_tags`, both
hold. Absent when empty, and then any tags.

Tagging.description:
Putting tags on, or taking them off: the actions of a tagging grant,
the same two for every kind that carries tags. Snake case on the
wire: `"tag"`, `"untag"`.

oneOf.description: Put tags on, as the kind's `tag` endpoint does.
Take tags off, as the kind's `untag` endpoint does.
